great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: The eligible Room Rent or Room Category applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is No limit, which means that there is no separate restriction on Room Charges incurred towards stay during Hospitalization
great.explanation: There is no limit on room rent charges during hospitalization, so you can choose any room without worrying about capping or extra out-of-pocket expenses.

great.name: ICU Charges
great.quote: Intensive Care Unit Charges (ICU Charges): The eligible ICU Charges applicable for the Insured Person under the Policy is No limit, which means that there is no separate restriction on ICU Charges incurred towards stay in ICU during Hospitalization.
great.explanation: ICU charges have no separate cap, meaning high ICU bills will be fully covered without restrictions.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year... Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness as well as different Illnesses.
great.explanation: The sum insured can be restored unlimited times per year and used even for the same illness, giving you extra coverage beyond your base limit.

great.name: No Claim Bonus
great.quote: enhance the Sum Insured by 50% flat... In the event of a Claim there is no impact on the accrual of Cumulative Bonus.
great.explanation: Your sum insured increases by 50% each year and this bonus is not lost even if you make a claim, so your coverage grows steadily.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: The Plus Benefit will be applicable only after exhaustion of Base Sum Insured.
great.explanation: An additional sum insured amount activates automatically after you use up your base sum insured, providing extra financial protection.

great.name: PED Waiting Period
great.quote: excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
great.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are excluded for 36 months, which is a reasonable waiting period common in the market.

great.name: Consumables
great.quote: If a claim has been accepted under this benefit, then the items which are not payable as per List- I, II, II and IV under Annexure I related to the particular claim, will become payable.
great.explanation: By opting for Claim Shield, many non-payable items like consumables become covered for that claim, reducing your out-of-pocket expenses.

good.name: Initial Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: There is a 30-day waiting period for illnesses except accidents, which is standard in the industry.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: Named illnesses are excluded for 24 months, a typical waiting period in most health insurance plans.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: For a period of 60 days immediately prior to the Insured Persons date of admission to the Hospital
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days before hospitalization are covered, which is a good standard benefit.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: For a period of 90 days immediately after the Insured Persons date of discharge from the hospital
good.explanation: Expenses for 90 days after hospital discharge are covered, providing good post-care support.

bad.name: Consumables Exclusion
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure 	I to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.explanation: Many common hospital consumables are excluded in the base plan, which can lead to significant out-of-pocket costs unless you opt for the Claim Shield add-on.

bad.name: Claim Intimation
bad.quote: the Company or the Assistance Service Provider shall be notified with full particulars within 48 hours from the date of occurrence of event
bad.explanation: You must inform the insurer within 48 hours of the event, which can be difficult in emergencies and may risk claim rejection if delayed.

bad.name: Claim Filing Deadline
bad.quote: Claim must be filed within 30 days from the date of discharge from the hospital
bad.explanation: Claims must be submitted within 30 days after discharge, which is strict and could complicate claim settlement if delayed.

bad.name: Domiciliary Exclusions
bad.quote: Any Medical Expenses incurred for the treatment in relation to any of the following diseases shall not be payable under this Benefit : ... Diabetes Mellitus... Hypertension... Asthma... All Psychiatric or Psychosomatic Disorders... Arthritis, Gout and Rheumatism.
bad.explanation: Home treatment is not covered for many common chronic diseases, limiting the usefulness of domiciliary hospitalization benefits.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: All Claims shall be payable subject to the terms, conditions, exclusions, sub-limits and wait periods of the Policy
bad.reference: General Conditions under Benefits Covered, point 3(III)
bad.explanation: Claims may be subject to disease-specific sub-limits which can cap payouts, potentially reducing coverage for certain illnesses.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: The Co-payment proportion (If opted) shall be borne by the Insured Person on each Claim
bad.reference: General Conditions under Benefits Covered, point 5 and Clause 3.2.29
bad.explanation: Co-pay appears optional and is not clearly stated for the base plan, so it is unclear if any mandatory co-pay applies by default.
